standard_prerequisites.use: Turns a monomorphism which is an immersion into an open immersion.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dominant rational maps and their composition (the definition of birationality)

core_obligations: Start from inverse dominant rational maps and shrink to affine opens making the composite an inclusion (proof lines 12911-12919).
Show the morphism between the opens is an immersion via the section-immersion lemma (proof lines 12919-12922).
Swap the roles of the two opens and use monomorphisms to obtain an open immersion, giving an isomorphic open in both schemes (proof lines 12922-12930).
Repeat the argument verbatim in the relative case (proof line 12931).
proof_roadmap: Open immersion and the isomorphic open (proof lines 12922-12931).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives the open-set characterisation of birationality for irreducible schemes, and its relative version over a base: two irreducible schemes are birational exactly when they have isomorphic nonempty opens, and likewise for birationality over $S$ and $S$-isomorphic nonempty opens. The proof starts from inverse dominant rational maps, shrinks to affine opens on which the composite is the inclusion of an open, uses the section-immersion lemma and the monomorphism form of immersions to show the morphisms between the opens are open immersions in both directions, and finishes with the isomorphic open subscheme; the relative statement is then the same argument.
